prompt: Nowadays, some employers think that formal academic qualifications are more important than life experience or personal qualities when they look for new employees. Why is it the case? Is it a positive or negative development
essay:
In recent decades, a degree has become an essential requirement when employers hire new employees. I believe this trend has arisen because of the improvement of modern education. This means that more people now have degrees, and employers use them as a quick sign of basic skill when there are many applicants for one job. In my view, this is largely a negative development.

Admittedly, a degree is an international standard for getting a job, especially in medicine, education and finance. Employers trust degrees because they may show basic knowledge, hard work, and the ability to finish a long course. For this reason, a degree serves as a convenient filter, simplifying headhunters’ search. Degrees vary by level—bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral—or by university prestige. However, this also means that degrees may become a standard requirement even for jobs where practical skills matter more.

In contrast, the drawbacks are substantial. By ignoring practical skills and personal characteristics, companies may miss good workers or make poor hiring choices. For example, an experienced salesperson without a degree may be rejected for a sales manager role, while a less capable graduate is hired; this can cost the firm clients and revenue. Similarly, a skilled cook without a degree may be overlooked for a head chef role, which can reduce a restaurant’s quality. This trend can leave skilled people feeling unfulfilled. Consequently, the negative repercussions outweigh the benefits, as a degree does not guarantee competence.

In conclusion, although degrees help employers screen candidates and show basic knowledge and commitment, this trend is predominantly negative because it undervalues practical experience and personal qualities. A balanced approach considering both degrees and real-world skills would be fairer and more effective.
